content.tex: In this investigation, lengths are given in centimetres. The area of a shape is A square centimetres and its perimeter is \(P\) centimetres.
This task investigates the dimensions of equable shapes. The shape is equable if A \(= P\) .
All the diagrams in this investigation are not to scale.
This rectangle is equable. Write down the calculations to show that A \(= 16.2\) and \(P = 16.2\) .

parts.label: b

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) For the rectangle in part (a) , the value of ( x – 2)( y – 2) is (4.5 – 2)(3.6 – 2) = 2.5 × 1.6 = 4. The rectangles in the table are equable. Use your answers to part (b) to complete the first two columns of the table. Calculate the value of ( x – 2)( y – 2) for each rectangle. content.tex: Use what you notice about the value of \((x - 2)(y - 2)\) in part (c) to find all the equable rectangles that have integer lengths and widths.

parts.text: The area, A , of a triangle is 2 1 × base × height.

content.tex: The area, A, of a triangle is \(\frac{1}{2} \times\) base \(\times\) height.
This right-angled triangle is equable. Write down the calculations to show that A \(= 23.4\) and \(P = 23.4\) .
